passage.title: Helping at the Store
passage.text:
Aling Nena owns a small sari-sari store beside the road. Her son Carlo helps every afternoon after school.

First, Carlo sweeps the front of the store. Then he arranges the candies, chips, and canned goods on the shelves. He puts the heavy cans on the bottom and the light chips on top so nothing falls.

One day, a customer bought ten pesos of rice and gave a twenty-peso bill. Carlo counted the change carefully. "Ten pesos," he said, and handed it over. The customer smiled. "You are a good helper."

At six o'clock, Aling Nena closed the store. She gave Carlo a cold soda. "For my hard-working boy," she said. Carlo drank it slowly and watched the tricycles pass. He was tired, but he felt useful. Tomorrow he would help again.
